subjects.name: Mathematik
subjects.description: Core subject from Klasse 1 to the Abitur, structured nationally by the KMK Bildungsstandards (end of Kl. 4; ESA/MSA for Sek I; Allgemeine Hochschulreife 2012 with grundlegendes and erhöhtes Anforderungsniveau) with Leitideen and process competences; Länder curricula set the grade placement. At the Gymnasium, Kl. 7–10 cover algebra, functions, geometry and stochastics; the Oberstufe is organised by the Sachgebiete Analysis, Lineare Algebra/Analytische Geometrie and Stochastik. Mathematik is a compulsory Abitur-relevant subject in every Land (in Bayern all students take it at erhöhtes Niveau).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Rational numbers
topics.description: Extend the negative integers to negative fractions and decimals, so that every fraction has an opposite number. Students order rational numbers on the number line, find the Betrag (absolute value) and the Gegenzahl, and see ℕ ⊂ ℤ ⊂ ℚ as a chain of number-range extensions.
evidence: Place numbers such as −2.5, −3/4 and 1 1/3 correctly on a number line
Order a mixed list of positive and negative fractions and decimals
State the absolute value and the opposite of a rational number and explain both on the number line
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} put −0.8, −3/4, 0.7 and −1 1/2 in order from smallest to largest, and explain why −0.8 is smaller than −3/4?

prerequisites.reason: Negative integers are extended to negative fractions
Fractions are placed on the number line
Fractions and decimals are compared

osMatches.note: os covers absolute value; ordering negative fractions is part of the German topic
positive fractions only

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Gym introduces integers in Jgst. 5 and handles negative fractions in Jgst. 6; NRW (G9) and most Länder extend to ℚ in Kl. 7.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Adding and subtracting rational numbers
topics.description: Add and subtract positive and negative fractions and decimals, using the rules for equal and opposite signs, the idea that subtracting a number means adding its opposite, and the Klammerregeln for expressions such as 5 − (−3).
evidence: Add two rational numbers with different signs, e.g. −3.5 + 1.2
Rewrite a subtraction of a negative number as an addition and calculate it
Model additions and subtractions with arrows on the number line or with account balances
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out −2/3 − (−1/2) and explain why the result is negative?

prerequisites.reason: Calculations use numbers of ℚ
Fraction addition is extended to signed fractions
Decimal addition is extended to signed decimals

osMatches.note: os stresses meaning in context rather than signed fraction arithmetic

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Multiplying and dividing rational numbers
topics.description: Multiply and divide signed fractions and decimals with the sign rules (minus times minus gives plus), justify the rules by continuing patterns or with the distributive law, and decide the sign of longer products and powers of negative numbers.
evidence: Multiply and divide rational numbers with correct signs
Explain with a pattern why (−3) · (−4) = 12
Decide the sign of a product with several negative factors or of a power such as (−2)⁵
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say without calculating whether (−1.5) · 4 · (−2) · (−0.5) is positive or negative, and why?

prerequisites.reason: Signs are already familiar from addition
Fraction multiplication is extended to signed numbers
Division by a fraction uses the reciprocal

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Arithmetic laws with signed numbers
topics.description: Use the commutative, associative and distributive laws and the order of operations in mixed calculations with positive and negative rational numbers, including brackets preceded by a minus sign, to calculate efficiently and correctly.
evidence: Evaluate a mixed expression with signed numbers, brackets and powers in the right order
Rearrange a sum of signed numbers to calculate more easily and name the law used
Find and correct a sign error in a worked calculation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} calculate −3 · (4 − 7) + (−2)² − 5 step by step and explain which rule they used at each step?

prerequisites.reason: All four operations with signed numbers are combined
The arithmetic laws are already known for positive numbers
Order of operations is extended to ℚ

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Percentage calculations
topics.description: Solve the three basic percentage tasks — find the Prozentwert, the Prozentsatz or the Grundwert — with the Dreisatz, the Prozentstreifen or the formula W = p % · G, and judge which quantity is unknown in an everyday situation.
evidence: Identify Grundwert, Prozentwert and Prozentsatz in a word problem
Calculate each of the three quantities when the other two are given
Represent a percentage problem with a percentage bar (Prozentstreifen) and check the result by estimation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If 18 of the 24 pupils in a class have a smartphone, can {{name}} work out the percentage — and then the number of pupils if 75 % of a school of 640 have one?

prerequisites.reason: Percentages as hundredths are introduced in Kl. 6
The Dreisatz is one standard solution method

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Gym introduces percentages in Jgst. 6 and deepens them in Jgst. 7; NRW, BW and most Länder teach the Grundaufgaben in Kl. 7.

topics.name: Percentage change and growth factors

Find the original price from the reduced price and the discount
Explain why +10 % followed by −10 % does not give the starting value

topics.name: Compound interest

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Square roots
topics.description: Understand √a as the non-negative number whose square is a, know the square roots of the square numbers up to 400, estimate roots between neighbouring whole numbers, and see why negative numbers have no square root in ℝ and why √(a²) = |a|.
evidence: State square roots of perfect squares and of numbers such as 0.09 or 1.44

topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find the point where f(x) = −x³ + 3x² + 1 rises most steeply, and explain why it is an inflection point?

prerequisites.reason: The second derivative extends the analysis of f′
The inflection tangent is set up

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Investigating functions systematically
topics.description: Carry out a complete investigation of a function: domain, symmetry, behaviour at infinity, zeros, extreme and inflection points, and sketch the graph; use digital tools sensibly and check results against the graph.
evidence: Investigate a polynomial function completely and sketch its graph
Use symmetry and end behaviour to reduce the work
Check a hand calculation with a plotter or CAS and explain discrepancies
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} investigate f(x) = ¼x⁴ − 2x² fully and draw an accurate sketch without a plotter?

prerequisites.reason: Inflection points are part of the investigation
End behaviour and symmetry of polynomials
Zeros are calculated

topics.laenderNotes: The 'Kurvendiskussion' as a fixed checklist is a German (and Austrian) school tradition; recent plans stress understanding and digital tools over routine.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Rational functions and asymptotes
topics.description: Investigate quotients of polynomials: domain, poles with and without change of sign, removable gaps, vertical and horizontal (or oblique) asymptotes, and sketch graphs from these features.
evidence: Find the domain, poles and vertical asymptotes of a rational function
Determine the horizontal asymptote from the degrees of numerator and denominator
Sketch the graph from its asymptotes, zeros and a few values
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find all asymptotes of f(x) = (2x + 1)/(x − 3) and sketch the graph?

prerequisites.reason: Asymptotes are limits
y = k/x is the simplest example
Domains of fraction terms are known

topics.laenderNotes: Mainly Bayern (Jgst. 8, 11 and 12 with the quotient rule, for all students) and the BW Leistungsfach; not part of the NRW, NI or Berlin/Brandenburg plans or the KMK standards.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Optimisation problems
topics.description: Solve optimisation problems in geometry and economics: set up a target function with a side condition, determine the sensible domain, find the global extremum with the derivative (including boundary values) and interpret the result.
evidence: Set up a target function using a side condition to eliminate a variable
Find the global optimum on the sensible domain, checking the boundaries
Interpret the optimum and discuss the model's assumptions
topics.assessmentPrompt: A can should hold 1 litre with as little metal as possible. Can {{name}} set up the problem and find the best radius?

prerequisites.reason: The optimum is a global extremum
Optimisation with parabolas is known
The side condition is solved for one variable

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Determining functions from conditions
topics.description: Reconstruct a polynomial function from given properties (points, extrema, inflection points, tangents, symmetry): translate each property into an equation for the coefficients and solve the resulting linear system, e.g. for road or roller-coaster transitions.
evidence: Translate verbal conditions into equations for the coefficients
Solve the resulting system and check all conditions
Model a smooth transition between two tracks with a polynomial
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find the cubic function whose graph has a high point at (1 | 4) and passes through the origin with slope 6?

prerequisites.reason: The conditions form a linear system
Conditions involve f′ and f″
The result is checked by investigating the function

topics.laenderNotes: 'Steckbriefaufgaben' are a typical German exam format; Bayern places parameter fitting in Jgst. 13 and simpler parabola fitting already in Jgst. 9.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Families of functions
topics.description: Investigate families of functions with a parameter (e.g. f_a(x) = x³ − ax): how the parameter changes the graph, dependence of zeros and extreme points on the parameter, common points of all graphs, and the curve on which all extreme points lie (Ortskurve).
evidence: Describe the effect of the parameter on the graphs using a slider tool
Calculate extreme points in dependence of the parameter
Find the locus (Ortskurve) of the extreme points or the points common to all graphs
topics.assessmentPrompt: For f_a(x) = x² − 2ax, can {{name}} find the vertex in terms of a and the curve on which all vertices lie?

prerequisites.reason: Each member of the family is investigated
Sliders show the effect of the parameter

topics.laenderNotes: NRW: Leistungskurs only; Bayern teaches families of functions to all students (all at eA level).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Combining and composing functions
topics.description: Build new functions as sums, products and compositions f(g(x)) of known functions, identify the inner and outer function of a composition, and use combined functions to describe contexts.
evidence: Write a given term as sum, product or composition of known functions
Identify inner and outer function, e.g. in e^(−0.5x) or (3x − 1)⁴
Form u(v(x)) and v(u(x)) and show that they differ
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write f(x) = √(4 − x²) as a composition and say which part is the inner function?

prerequisites.reason: Functions are combined
Transformations are special compositions

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: The natural exponential function
topics.nameDe: Natürliche Exponentialfunktion und Eulersche Zahl e
topics.description: Find the special base e ≈ 2.718 for which the exponential function equals its own derivative, (eˣ)′ = eˣ, write any exponential function as e^(kx), and differentiate e^(kx) and a · e^(kx).
evidence: Explain why the exponential function with base e is its own derivative
Differentiate functions such as 3e^(2x) or e^(−0.1x)
Rewrite a growth function a · bˣ in the form a · e^(kx)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what is special about the number e, and differentiate f(x) = 5e^(−0.2x)?

prerequisites.reason: eˣ is a special exponential function
The derivative of exponential functions is studied
Converting bˣ to e^(kx) needs a logarithm

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Product rule
topics.description: Differentiate products of functions with the product rule (u · v)′ = u′v + uv′, justify the rule with an area model or the difference quotient, and apply it to products of polynomials, exponential and trigonometric functions.
evidence: Differentiate products such as x² · e^x and (x − 1) · e^(−x)
Show that the product rule gives the same result as expanding for two polynomials
Explain why (u · v)′ is not u′ · v′
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} differentiate f(x) = x · e^(−x) and use the result to find where the graph has its high point?

prerequisites.reason: Product rule extends the basic rules
Typical products contain e-functions

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Chain rule
topics.description: Differentiate compositions with the chain rule (u(v(x)))′ = u′(v(x)) · v′(x) — 'outer derivative times inner derivative' — also for non-linear inner functions, and combine it with the product rule.
evidence: Differentiate compositions such as (2x² + 1)⁵, e^(x²) and √(1 − x)
Combine chain and product rule, e.g. for x · e^(−x²)
Justify the chain rule for a linear inner function with the difference quotient
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} differentiate f(x) = e^(−0.5x²) and explain what 'inner derivative' means here?

prerequisites.reason: The rule differentiates compositions
Outer and inner derivatives use the basic rules
Both rules are combined

topics.laenderNotes: KMK: eA only. In practice basic courses in NRW, NI, BW (Basisfach) and Berlin/Brandenburg use the chain rule for linear (Berlin/Brandenburg also quadratic) inner functions such as e^(kx); Bayern teaches the general rule to all.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Investigating composite exponential functions
topics.description: Investigate functions such as f(x) = x · e^(−x), (x² − 1) · eˣ or e^x + e^(−x): zeros via the zero-product rule (eˣ is never zero), derivatives with product rule and linear chain rule, extrema, inflection points, and limits using that eˣ dominates every power.
evidence: Find the zeros of a product with an exponential factor and justify why eˣ ≠ 0
Determine extreme and inflection points of a composite exponential function
Describe the behaviour for x → ±∞ using 'e beats every power'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find the zeros, extrema and long-term behaviour of f(x) = (x − 2) · eˣ?

prerequisites.reason: Derivatives of products are needed
The exponential part is differentiated
The investigation follows the usual steps

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Exponential and bounded growth models
topics.nameDe: Wachstumsmodelle mit e-Funktionen (exponentielles und begrenztes Wachstum)
topics.description: Model growth and decay with f(t) = a · e^(kt), determine k from data or a half-life, use the derivative as growth rate (f′ = k · f), and describe bounded growth towards a limit S with f(t) = S − c · e^(−kt) (e.g. cooling, medication levels).
evidence: Find k from two data points or a half-life and interpret its sign
Interpret f′(t) = k · f(t) as 'growth rate proportional to the amount'
Set up and interpret a bounded growth model for cooling coffee
topics.assessmentPrompt: Coffee at 80 °C cools in a 20 °C room. Can {{name}} explain why S − c·e^(−kt) fits better than a pure exponential decay, and what S means?

prerequisites.reason: Models use the natural exponential function
Choosing a model type is known from Kl. 10
k is calculated with a logarithm

externalPrerequisites.subject: Physik
externalPrerequisites.reason: Decay is a standard application of exponential models

topics.laenderNotes: NRW names bounded growth for the Grundkurs; logistic growth and differential equations appear only in some Leistungskurse.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Inverse functions
topics.description: Decide when a function can be inverted (strict monotonicity), find the inverse function algebraically and graphically as a reflection in y = x, using the square root function as inverse of x² on x ≥ 0, and relate the derivatives of a function and its inverse.
evidence: Explain why x² can only be inverted on a restricted domain
Find the term of the inverse of a linear or root function and sketch both graphs
Differentiate √x as the inverse of x² (or as x^(1/2))
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why f(x) = x² has no inverse on all of ℝ, and give the inverse for x ≥ 0 with its graph?

prerequisites.reason: Strict monotonicity guarantees invertibility
The square root inverts squaring
Reflection in y = x is a graph transformation

topics.laenderNotes: NRW Grundkurs uses the root function as example; Bayern Jgst. 12; in BW only the Leistungsfach (G9 plan).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: The natural logarithm function
topics.description: Introduce ln as the inverse function of eˣ, know its graph and properties, its derivative (ln x)′ = 1/x, use ln|x| as an antiderivative of 1/x, and solve equations with e and ln.
evidence: Sketch ln x as the reflection of eˣ and state domain, zero and asymptote
Differentiate functions containing ln, e.g. x · ln x
Use ln to integrate 1/x and to solve e^(2x) = 5
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why ln x is only defined for x > 0, and calculate the area under 1/x from 1 to e?

prerequisites.reason: ln inverts the e-function
ln is an inverse function
Logarithms are known from Kl. 10
Derivatives of ln compositions use the chain rule

topics.laenderNotes: KMK: ln function eA only; in basic courses ln is used just as a number to solve exponential equations. Bayern teaches the ln function to all.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Derivatives of sine and cosine
topics.description: Find graphically that sin′ = cos and cos′ = −sin, differentiate functions such as a · sin(bx) + d, and use the derivatives to analyse periodic models (e.g. maximum rate of change of day length).
evidence: Explain by graphical differentiation why the derivative of sin is cos
Differentiate functions of the form a · sin(bx + c) + d
Find when a periodic quantity changes fastest
topics.assessmentPrompt: If day length is modelled by L(t) = 12 + 4.5 · sin(2πt/365), can {{name}} work out on which day it changes fastest?

prerequisites.reason: Sine models with parameters are differentiated
Graphical differentiation reveals the derivative

topics.laenderNotes: NRW Grundkurs: derivatives of sin and cos; general a·sin(bx + c) + d only in the Leistungskurs.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Differentiability and linear approximation
topics.description: Interpret the derivative as the slope of the best linear approximation near a point (the tangent replaces the graph locally), estimate function values with it, and recognise points where a function is not differentiable (kinks, jumps).
evidence: Use the tangent to estimate f(x₀ + h) for small h and judge the error
Explain differentiability as 'locally linear' with zooming
Show that |x| is not differentiable at 0 using left and right difference quotients
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use the tangent at x = 4 to estimate √4.1 without a calculator, and explain why the estimate is good?

prerequisites.reason: The tangent is the linear approximation
Left and right limits are compared

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Reconstructing totals from rates of change
topics.description: Reconstruct a total change from a rate (flow, speed, growth rate) as the oriented area between the rate graph and the x-axis, approximate it with rectangle sums (Produktsummen, Ober- und Untersummen), and interpret areas below the axis as decreases.
evidence: Calculate the volume that flowed into a tank from a piecewise constant inflow rate
Approximate a total change with lower and upper sums
Interpret areas below the axis as negative changes of the stock
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given a graph of the water inflow rate in litres per minute, can {{name}} estimate how much water is in the tank after 10 minutes if it started with 50 litres?

prerequisites.reason: Rate and stock are related like f′ and f
Areas under graphs are approximated with rectangles and trapezia

externalPrerequisites.subject: Physik
externalPrerequisites.concept: distance travelled as the area under a velocity–time graph
externalPrerequisites.reason: Motion is the classic context for reconstruction

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern treats integration in Jgst. 13; NRW in the Qualifikationsphase (Kl. 12).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: The definite integral
topics.description: Define the definite integral as the limit of rectangle sums, read it as an oriented area (Flächenbilanz) and as a reconstructed total, and use properties such as additivity over intervals and linearity.
evidence: Explain the integral as the limit of upper and lower sums
Calculate simple integrals as oriented areas from a graph
Use additivity and linearity to simplify an integral
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the integral of sin x from 0 to 2π is zero, even though the graph encloses area with the x-axis?

prerequisites.reason: The integral formalises reconstruction
The integral is a limit of sums

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Antiderivatives
topics.description: Find antiderivatives by reversing the differentiation rules — power rule, sum and factor rule, e^(kx), sin and cos, and linear substitution — and understand that antiderivatives differ only by a constant.
evidence: Find antiderivatives of polynomials and of e^(kx) and sin(bx)
Check an antiderivative by differentiating it
Find the antiderivative that passes through a given point
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find an antiderivative of f(x) = 3x² − 4e^(2x) and check it by differentiating?

prerequisites.reason: Antiderivatives reverse the rules
Exponential functions are integrated
Sine and cosine are integrated

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus
topics.description: Understand the integral function x ↦ ∫ₐˣ f(t) dt, justify geometrically that its derivative is f, and use the main theorem ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a) to calculate integrals with antiderivatives.
evidence: Explain with a strip of area why the integral function has derivative f
Calculate definite integrals with F(b) − F(a)
Sketch an integral function from the graph of f
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain, with a thin strip under the graph, why the rate at which the area grows equals the function value?

prerequisites.reason: The theorem links the integral with derivatives
Integrals are calculated with antiderivatives

topics.laenderNotes: Leistungskurse (NRW, Bayern) justify the theorem more formally; basic courses geometrically.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Areas between graphs
topics.description: Calculate areas between a graph and the x-axis (splitting at zeros) and between two graphs (integrating the difference between intersection points), and solve related problems such as finding a boundary so that an area has a given size.
evidence: Calculate an area enclosed by a graph and the x-axis that lies partly below the axis
Calculate the area between two graphs from their intersection points
Find a parameter so that an area takes a given value
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} calculate the area enclosed by f(x) = x² and g(x) = x + 2?

prerequisites.reason: Areas are calculated with antiderivatives
Boundaries are zeros or intersection points

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Integrals in context
topics.description: Use integrals with antiderivatives to answer questions in contexts — total quantity from a rate, stock at a given time from an initial value, and the average value of a function over an interval — and interpret results with units.
evidence: Calculate a stock at time t from initial value and rate with an integral
Calculate and interpret the average value of a function over an interval
State the units of an integral in context (e.g. (litres/min) · min = litres)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If the inflow rate into a reservoir is r(t) = 20 + 6t − 0.3t² m³/h, can {{name}} work out how much water flows in during the first 10 hours and the average rate?

prerequisites.reason: Integrals are evaluated with the theorem
The meaning of an integral in context is known

topics.laenderNotes: The mean value of a function is named in the BW Leistungsfach and Bayern; elsewhere it appears as an application.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Volumes of revolution
topics.description: Calculate the volume of a solid formed by rotating a graph about the x-axis with V = π ∫ₐᵇ (f(x))² dx, derived from thin cylindrical discs, and model containers such as vases or barrels.
evidence: Derive the volume formula from discs (cylinders) of thickness Δx
Calculate the volume of a cone or paraboloid by rotation and check it
Model a vase by rotating a given profile curve
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} confirm the cone formula V = ⅓πr²h by rotating the line y = (r/h)·x about the x-axis?

prerequisites.reason: The volume is a definite integral
Thin discs are cylinders
Antiderivatives of squared compositions

topics.laenderNotes: Leistungskurs only in NRW, NI, BW and Berlin/Brandenburg; Bayern teaches it to all students.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Improper integrals
topics.description: Calculate integrals over unbounded intervals or of functions with a pole as limits of ordinary integrals, and decide whether an infinitely long region has a finite area (e.g. under 1/x² versus 1/x).
evidence: Write an improper integral as a limit and evaluate it
Show that the area under 1/x² from 1 to ∞ is finite but under 1/x is not
Interpret a finite improper integral in a context (e.g. total amount of a decaying emission)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how an area that stretches infinitely far to the right can still be finite, using f(x) = e^(−x)?

prerequisites.reason: Areas are calculated with integrals
The integral is a limit
1/x needs ln as antiderivative

topics.laenderNotes: Leistungskurs only in NRW, NI, BW and Berlin/Brandenburg; Bayern teaches it to all students.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Points in a 3D coordinate system
topics.description: Describe positions in space with three coordinates (x₁, x₂, x₃), draw points, edges and simple solids in an oblique drawing of the 3D coordinate system, and read coordinates of vertices of cuboids and pyramids.
evidence: Plot points with three coordinates in an oblique 3D drawing
Give the coordinates of all vertices of a cuboid placed in the system
Explain why one point in a 2D drawing can stand for many points in space
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a cuboid with one corner at the origin and edges 4, 3 and 2 in a 3D coordinate system and give the coordinates of all eight corners?

prerequisites.reason: The 2D coordinate system is extended by a third axis
Oblique drawings of solids are known

topics.laenderNotes: NRW and BW (G9 plan) start vectors in Kl. 11; Bayern in Jgst. 12; Berlin/Brandenburg and NI in the Qualifikationsphase.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Vectors as translations
topics.description: Understand a vector as a translation (the class of all arrows with the same length and direction), write vectors as columns, and use position vectors of points and connecting vectors AB⃗ = B⃗ − A⃗.
evidence: Explain why many arrows represent the same vector
Calculate the connecting vector between two points
Find the image of a point under a translation given by a vector
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find the vector from A(1 | 2 | 0) to B(4 | −1 | 3) and use it to shift C(0 | 0 | 5)?

prerequisites.reason: Vectors are written with coordinates
Translations are known from Kl. 6

externalPrerequisites.subject: Physik
externalPrerequisites.concept: forces and velocities as directed quantities with magnitude and direction

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Vector addition and scalar multiplication
topics.nameDe: Rechnen mit Vektoren: Addition, Vervielfachung, Linearkombination
topics.description: Add and subtract vectors (chaining arrows), multiply vectors by real numbers, form linear combinations, and use these operations to find midpoints, centroids and fourth vertices of parallelograms.
evidence: Add, subtract and scale vectors in coordinates and as arrows
Calculate the midpoint of a segment and the fourth vertex of a parallelogram
Express a vector as a linear combination of given vectors
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given three vertices of a parallelogram ABCD, can {{name}} find D with vectors and explain the idea with a sketch?

prerequisites.reason: Operations are defined for vectors

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Length of a vector and distance between points
topics.nameDe: Betrag eines Vektors und Abstand zweier Punkte
topics.description: Calculate the length (Betrag) of a vector with the spatial Pythagorean theorem, the distance between two points, and unit vectors, and use lengths to classify triangles and quadrilaterals in space.
evidence: Calculate the length of a vector in space
Calculate the distance between two points and check whether a triangle is isosceles
Find a vector of given length in a given direction
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} decide whether the triangle with corners A(1 | 0 | 2), B(3 | 4 | 2) and C(5 | 0 | 2) is isosceles?

prerequisites.reason: The length of a vector is calculated
The formula is the spatial Pythagorean theorem

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Collinearity and linear dependence
topics.description: Check whether two vectors are collinear (one is a multiple of the other) and whether three points lie on a line, and — for three vectors — whether they are coplanar (linearly dependent), solving the corresponding linear system.
evidence: Decide whether two vectors are collinear
Check whether three given points lie on one line
Decide with a linear system whether three vectors lie in one plane
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show that the points A(1 | 2 | 3), B(3 | 3 | 5) and C(7 | 5 | 9) lie on one straight line?

prerequisites.reason: Collinearity means one vector is a multiple of the other
Linear dependence of three vectors leads to a linear system

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Gaussian elimination
topics.nameDe: Lineare Gleichungssysteme mit dem Gauß-Verfahren lösen
topics.description: Solve linear systems with three (or more) unknowns by Gaussian elimination into triangular form, also in matrix notation, and interpret the solution set: unique, empty or infinitely many solutions described with a parameter.
evidence: Solve a 3×3 system without technology by transforming it to triangular form
Recognise from the triangular form whether there is no or infinitely many solutions
Describe an infinite solution set with a parameter
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} solve a system of three equations with three unknowns by elimination and show that a second system has no solution?

prerequisites.reason: Elimination is known for 2×2 systems

topics.laenderNotes: NRW: algorithmic method for at most three unknowns in the Qualifikationsphase; BW also in matrix notation; Bayern solves 3×3 systems by substitution in Jgst. 9 and teaches the Gauß algorithm only in the optional Vertiefungskurs.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Lines in vector form
topics.description: Describe straight lines and segments in space by x⃗ = p⃗ + t · u⃗ (support and direction vector), set up the equation through two points, check whether a point lies on a line and describe motions along lines (e.g. flight paths).
evidence: Set up the equation of a line through two points
Check with a parameter whether a point lies on a line or segment
Interpret the parameter as time in a motion problem
topics.assessmentPrompt: A plane flies from A(0 | 0 | 1) in direction (2 | 3 | 0.5) per minute. Can {{name}} set up its path and say where it is after 4 minutes?

prerequisites.reason: Points on the line are linear combinations
Lines in the plane are known from Kl. 8

topics.laenderNotes: NRW already in the Einführungsphase (Kl. 11); Bayern in Jgst. 13.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Relative position of two lines
topics.description: Decide whether two lines in space are identical, parallel, intersecting or skew by checking collinearity of the direction vectors and solving the system for a common point, and calculate intersection points.
evidence: Use the direction vectors to separate parallel/identical from other cases
Solve the system to find the intersection point or show that the lines are skew
Explain what 'skew' means and why it cannot happen in the plane
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} decide whether the flight paths of two planes cross, and if not, whether they are parallel or skew?

prerequisites.reason: Lines are given in parametric form
The common point is found from a linear system
Parallel lines have collinear direction vectors

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Dot product and orthogonality
topics.description: Calculate the dot product of two vectors, interpret it geometrically (a⃗ · b⃗ = |a⃗| · |b⃗| · cos φ), and use a⃗ · b⃗ = 0 to test and construct perpendicular vectors.
evidence: Calculate dot products in coordinates
Use the dot product to test whether two vectors are orthogonal
Find a vector orthogonal to two given vectors with a linear system
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} check whether the triangle with corners A(2 | 1 | 0), B(4 | 5 | 2) and C(6 | 0 | 1) has a right angle, using the dot product?

prerequisites.reason: The geometric meaning uses lengths
The cosine of obtuse angles is negative
The product is calculated from coordinates

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Angles between vectors and lines
topics.nameDe: Winkel zwischen Vektoren und Schnittwinkel von Geraden
topics.description: Calculate the angle between two vectors with cos φ = (a⃗ · b⃗)/(|a⃗| · |b⃗|), the interior angles of triangles in space and the intersection angle of two lines (taking the acute angle).
evidence: Calculate the angle between two vectors
Calculate the interior angles of a triangle in space
Calculate the angle at which two intersecting lines meet
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} calculate the angle at which two crossing roads, given as lines in space, meet?

prerequisites.reason: The angle formula uses the dot product
Intersecting lines are needed for intersection angles

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Cross product
topics.description: Calculate the cross product of two vectors, use it to find a vector perpendicular to both (e.g. a normal vector of a plane), and use its length for areas of parallelograms and triangles and, with the dot product, volumes of pyramids.
evidence: Calculate a⃗ × b⃗ and check that it is orthogonal to both vectors
Calculate the area of a triangle in space with the cross product
Calculate the volume of a pyramid with base triangle and apex
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use the cross product to find the area of the triangle with corners A(1 | 0 | 0), B(0 | 2 | 0) and C(0 | 0 | 3)?

prerequisites.reason: Orthogonality is checked with the dot product
Areas are lengths of the cross product

topics.laenderNotes: Taught to all students in Bayern and in BW (Basis- and Leistungsfach); not part of the NRW, NI (Gymnasium) or Berlin/Brandenburg plans, nor of the KMK standards.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Planes in vector form
topics.description: Describe planes by x⃗ = p⃗ + r · u⃗ + s · v⃗ with a support vector and two non-collinear direction vectors, set up the equation through three points and check whether a point lies in a plane.
evidence: Set up the parametric equation of a plane through three points
Explain why the two direction vectors must not be collinear
Check with a linear system whether a point lies in the plane
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} set up the equation of the roof plane of a house from three corner points and check whether a fourth corner lies in it?

prerequisites.reason: Planes extend the parametric form of lines
Direction vectors must be non-collinear
Point tests lead to linear systems

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Normal and coordinate form of a plane
topics.description: Describe a plane by a normal vector and a point (Normalenform) and by an equation ax₁ + bx₂ + cx₃ = d (Koordinatenform), convert between the forms, read the normal vector and draw the plane using its intercepts with the axes (Spurpunkte).
evidence: Set up the coordinate form from a point and a normal vector
Convert a parametric form into coordinate form
Find the axis intercepts and sketch the plane
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 2x₁ + 3x₂ + 6x₃ = 12 is a plane, draw it from its axis intercepts and give a normal vector?

prerequisites.reason: A normal vector is orthogonal to the plane
Forms are converted into each other
A normal vector can be found with the cross product

topics.laenderNotes: NRW Grundkurs: coordinate form with normal vector, Normalenform only in the Leistungskurs; NI gA uses only the parametric form.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Angles between lines and planes
topics.nameDe: Schnittwinkel von Gerade und Ebene sowie zweier Ebenen
topics.description: Calculate the angle between a line and a plane (using the sine with the normal vector) and between two planes (angle between the normal vectors), and apply this to roofs, ramps or light rays.
evidence: Calculate the angle between a line and a plane
Calculate the angle between two planes from their normal vectors
Interpret an intersection angle in a context (e.g. roof pitch)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} calculate the pitch of a roof given as a plane relative to the horizontal ground plane x₃ = 0?

prerequisites.reason: Angles use normal vectors
Angles between vectors are calculated

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Line and plane: position and intersection point
topics.description: Decide whether a line lies in a plane, is parallel to it or intersects it, and calculate the intersection point by substituting the line into the coordinate form, e.g. for a shadow or a light ray hitting a surface.
evidence: Substitute a line into a coordinate equation and interpret the result
Calculate the intersection point of a line and a plane
Use the normal vector to recognise a line parallel to the plane
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find where the shadow of the top of a mast falls on a sloping hillside plane, given the direction of the sun's rays?

prerequisites.reason: The plane is given in coordinate form
Line positions are already analysed

topics.laenderNotes: KMK: eA only. NRW also requires the intersection point line–plane in the Grundkurs; Bayern teaches it to all.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Relative position of two planes
topics.description: Decide whether two planes are identical, parallel or intersecting, and calculate the line of intersection by solving the system of their equations with a parameter.
evidence: Compare normal vectors to detect parallel or identical planes
Calculate the line of intersection of two planes
Interpret the intersection line in a context (e.g. ridge of a roof)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} calculate the ridge line where two roof planes of a house meet?

prerequisites.reason: The approach extends line–plane analysis
The intersection line is the solution set of a system

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Distance from a point to a plane
topics.description: Calculate the distance of a point from a plane with the Hesse normal form (using the unit normal vector) or with a perpendicular line and its foot point, and use it for heights of pyramids or safety distances.
evidence: Convert a coordinate equation into the Hesse normal form
Calculate the distance of a point from a plane in two ways
Calculate the height and volume of a pyramid with this distance
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} calculate how high the apex of a tent lies above a sloping ground plane?

prerequisites.reason: The normal vector gives the shortest direction
A unit normal vector is needed
The foot point is an intersection of line and plane

topics.laenderNotes: KMK: eA only; BW Basisfach and the Berlin/Brandenburg Grundkurs also include point–plane distance; NI gA only point–point.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Distances from lines and between skew lines
topics.nameDe: Abstand Punkt–Gerade und Abstand windschiefer Geraden
topics.description: Calculate the distance of a point from a line (with an auxiliary plane or by minimising a distance function) and the shortest distance between two skew lines, and interpret closest-approach problems (e.g. two flight paths).
evidence: Calculate the distance between a point and a line with an auxiliary plane or the dot product
Calculate the distance between two skew lines
Interpret the minimum distance of two planes in flight as a safety question
topics.assessmentPrompt: Two planes fly on skew straight paths. Can {{name}} work out the smallest distance between the two paths?

prerequisites.reason: Auxiliary planes reduce the problem
The shortest connection is orthogonal to the lines
Skew lines are recognised first

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Matrices for multistage processes
topics.description: Describe processes such as customer migration or population stages by a transition graph and a transition matrix, calculate the next state by matrix–vector multiplication and earlier states by solving a system or with the inverse matrix.
evidence: Set up a transition matrix from a transition graph or a table
Calculate the state after one and two steps with matrix–vector multiplication
Multiply two matrices and interpret the product as two steps of a process
topics.assessmentPrompt: Each year 10 % of the customers of shop A switch to shop B and 20 % of B's switch to A. Can {{name}} set up the matrix and work out the shares after two years?

prerequisites.reason: States are vectors
Earlier states lead to linear systems
Transition probabilities follow the path rules

topics.laenderNotes: Only for Länder choosing the KMK alternative A1 (matrices). Of the Länder checked, none makes transition matrices compulsory: NRW dropped them in 2023, Bayern and Berlin offer them only in optional courses, NI eA uses matrices only for projections.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Long-term behaviour of processes
topics.description: Use powers of a transition matrix for many steps, investigate whether the process approaches a stable distribution (limit matrix), and calculate a fixed vector (stationary distribution) by solving M · v⃗ = v⃗.
evidence: Calculate high matrix powers with a digital tool and describe the trend
Calculate a fixed vector by solving a linear system
Interpret a stationary distribution and an absorbing state in the context
topics.assessmentPrompt: For the customer-switching matrix, can {{name}} work out the market shares the two shops will settle at in the long run?

prerequisites.reason: Long-term behaviour extends the step-by-step process
The fixed vector is a solution of a linear system

topics.laenderNotes: Only in Länder choosing KMK alternative A1; in Bayern part of the optional Vertiefungskurs (Jgst. 12).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Reversing tree diagrams (Bayes)
topics.nameDe: Umgekehrtes Baumdiagramm und Satz von Bayes
topics.description: Reverse the order of the stages in a tree diagram (via the two-way table or Bayes' formula) to answer questions such as 'How likely is it that a person with a positive test is really ill?', and explain the role of the base rate.
evidence: Draw the reversed tree diagram from a given tree via a two-way table
Calculate a 'reverse' conditional probability with Bayes' formula
Explain why a rare illness leads to many false positives even with a good test
topics.assessmentPrompt: An illness affects 1 % of people; a test is 98 % reliable either way. Can {{name}} work out how likely it is that someone who tests positive is ill — and explain the surprisingly low answer?

prerequisites.reason: Conditional probabilities are reversed
The two-way table links both tree diagrams

topics.laenderNotes: Bayes' formula is named explicitly only in some plans; most work with the reversed tree or natural frequencies.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Stochastic independence
topics.description: Define two events as independent when P(A ∩ B) = P(A) · P(B), or equivalently P_A(B) = P(B), check independence in two-way tables and tree diagrams, and distinguish stochastic independence from causal independence.
evidence: Test two events for independence with the product formula
Recognise independence in a tree diagram from equal conditional probabilities
Explain with an example why dependence does not prove a causal link
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a survey, can {{name}} check from the two-way table whether 'wears glasses' and 'is left-handed' are stochastically independent?

prerequisites.reason: Independence is defined with conditional probabilities
Independence is checked in two-way tables

topics.laenderNotes: NRW introduces independence already in Kl. 9–10 and checks it again in the Qualifikationsphase; Bayern Jgst. 11.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Counting arrangements and selections
topics.description: Count ordered arrangements with n! and n!/(n − k)!, count unordered selections with the binomial coefficient (n über k), and use the urn model to decide which counting rule fits (with/without order, with/without replacement).
evidence: Count arrangements of n objects with the factorial
Calculate a binomial coefficient and explain it as the number of k-element subsets
Calculate the probability of '6 aus 49' type lottery events
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out how many different tips there are in the German lottery '6 aus 49' and the chance of getting all six right?

prerequisites.reason: Counting builds on the product rule
Urn models without replacement are counted

topics.laenderNotes: Berlin teaches factorials and binomial coefficients in the Einführungsphase; Bayern Jgst. 12; NRW only in the Leistungskurs (Grundkurs uses the calculator).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Random variables and probability distributions
topics.description: Assign numbers to the outcomes of a random experiment (e.g. winnings, number of hits) as a random variable X, tabulate and draw its probability distribution as a histogram, and use the axioms that probabilities are non-negative and add up to 1.
evidence: Define a suitable random variable for a game and list its values
Set up the probability distribution in a table and check that it sums to 1
Draw and interpret the distribution as a histogram
topics.assessmentPrompt: Two dice are thrown and X is the larger number shown. Can {{name}} set up the probability distribution of X?

prerequisites.reason: Probabilities of values are found with path rules
A random variable assigns numbers to outcomes

topics.laenderNotes: BW's G9 plan moves the binomial distribution, and with it random variables, to Kl. 11.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Expected value
topics.description: Calculate the expected value E(X) as the probability-weighted mean of the values, interpret it as the long-run average, and use it to decide whether a game is fair or to set a fair stake.
evidence: Calculate E(X) from a probability distribution
Decide whether a game is fair and adjust the payout to make it fair
Interpret the expected value as the average over many repetitions
topics.assessmentPrompt: At a school fair you pay €2 to spin a wheel that pays €10 with probability 0.1 and €1 with probability 0.5. Can {{name}} decide who profits in the long run?

prerequisites.reason: The expected value summarises a distribution
The expected value generalises the mean

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Variance and standard deviation
topics.description: Measure the spread of a random variable around its expected value by variance and standard deviation, compare distributions with equal mean but different risk, and relate them to the empirical standard deviation of a data sample.
evidence: Calculate variance and standard deviation of a random variable
Compare two games with the same expected value by their risk
Calculate and interpret the empirical standard deviation of a sample
topics.assessmentPrompt: Two games both have expected winnings of €0. Can {{name}} use the standard deviation to explain which one is riskier?

prerequisites.reason: Spread is measured around the expected value
The standard deviation is a square root
Spread of data is known from box plots

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Bernoulli trials and Bernoulli chains
topics.description: Recognise experiments with exactly two outcomes (hit/miss) as Bernoulli trials and n independent repetitions with constant p as a Bernoulli chain, and judge whether a real situation (e.g. quality control, multiple-choice guessing) can be modelled this way.
evidence: Identify n, p and 'hit' for a given situation
Check the conditions (two outcomes, independence, constant p) in a context
Explain why drawing without replacement from a small urn is not a Bernoulli chain
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} decide whether guessing on a 10-question multiple-choice test with 4 options each is a Bernoulli chain, and state n and p?

prerequisites.reason: The trials must be independent
Paths of a Bernoulli chain are multiplied

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Binomial distribution
topics.description: Calculate the probability of exactly k hits in a Bernoulli chain with Bernoulli's formula P(X = k) = (n über k) · pᵏ · (1 − p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ, explain each factor with the tree diagram, and describe the shape of binomial histograms for different n and p.
evidence: Calculate P(X = k) with the formula and with a calculator function
Explain the meaning of the binomial coefficient and the powers in the formula
Describe how the histogram changes with n and p
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} calculate the probability of exactly 3 sixes in 10 throws of a die, and explain where each part of the formula comes from?

prerequisites.reason: The distribution describes the number of hits
The binomial coefficient counts the paths
The number of hits is a random variable

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Cumulative binomial probabilities
topics.description: Calculate probabilities for 'at most', 'at least', 'more than' and 'between' with the cumulative binomial distribution from tables or a calculator, translating each phrase correctly (e.g. P(X ≥ k) = 1 − P(X ≤ k − 1)).
evidence: Translate verbal conditions into inequalities for X
Calculate P(X ≥ k) and P(a ≤ X ≤ b) with cumulative values
Spot and correct the typical off-by-one error
topics.assessmentPrompt: A machine produces 5 % defective parts. Can {{name}} calculate the probability that a box of 50 contains more than 3 defective parts?

prerequisites.reason: Cumulative values sum single probabilities
Verbal conditions become inequalities

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Mean and spread of the binomial distribution
topics.description: Use μ = n · p and σ = √(n · p · (1 − p)) for binomially distributed variables, relate them to the position and width of the histogram, and interpret them in contexts.
evidence: Calculate μ and σ for a binomial distribution
Explain how μ and σ change when n is multiplied by 4
Use μ and σ to describe where most results are expected
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out how many heads to expect in 400 coin tosses and roughly how much the result usually varies?

prerequisites.reason: The formulas describe binomial distributions
σ is the standard deviation of X

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Problem solving with the binomial distribution
topics.description: Solve inverse problems with the binomial distribution: find the minimum number of trials n for a required probability ('Dreimal-mindestens-Aufgabe'), find the largest or smallest k for a given probability, and judge whether an observed result is unusual for an assumed p.
evidence: Find the minimum n so that P(at least one hit) exceeds a given value, using logarithms or a table
Find the smallest k with P(X ≤ k) ≥ 0.95 from a cumulative table
Judge whether an observed number of hits is plausible for a claimed p
topics.assessmentPrompt: How many times must you buy a scratch card with a 5 % win rate to have at least a 90 % chance of winning at least once? Can {{name}} work it out?

prerequisites.reason: Inverse problems use cumulative probabilities
The minimum n is found with logarithms

topics.laenderNotes: The 'Dreimal-mindestens-Aufgabe' is a standard German exam type.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Prediction intervals and sigma rules
topics.description: Predict in which interval the number or proportion of hits in a sample will lie with a given probability (e.g. 95 %), using cumulative tables or the σ-rules (μ ± 1.96σ), and use this to decide whether a sample is compatible with an assumed probability.
evidence: Determine a 95 % prediction interval with a table or the σ-rules
Use the interval to judge whether a sample result fits an assumed p
Explain how the interval for the relative frequency shrinks with growing n
topics.assessmentPrompt: A party is said to have 30 % support. Can {{name}} work out which numbers of supporters in a poll of 1,000 people would be compatible with this claim?

prerequisites.reason: Intervals are centred at μ with width based on σ
Interval probabilities are cumulative

topics.laenderNotes: Berlin/Brandenburg teach k-σ intervals in all courses; NI gA works with tables (σ-neighbourhoods eA); NRW: σ-rules and prediction intervals Leistungskurs only.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Confidence intervals
topics.description: Estimate an unknown probability p from a sample: find all p for which the observed result lies in the prediction interval (confidence interval), interpret the confidence level correctly and determine the sample size needed for a given accuracy.
evidence: Determine a 95 % confidence interval for p from a sample result
Explain correctly what '95 % confidence' means and does not mean
Calculate the sample size needed for a margin of error of ±2 percentage points
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a poll 420 of 1,200 people support a proposal. Can {{name}} give a 95 % confidence interval for the true share and explain what it tells us?

prerequisites.reason: Confidence intervals invert prediction intervals
Interval limits can lead to quadratic equations

topics.laenderNotes: KMK alternative B1 (eA). NRW Leistungskurs, NI eA; Länder choosing hypothesis tests (B2) may omit it.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: One-sided significance tests
topics.description: Test a claim about a probability p: formulate null and alternative hypothesis, choose significance level and sample size, determine the rejection region with the cumulative binomial distribution, make a decision from the sample and interpret it carefully.
evidence: Formulate H₀ and H₁ for a claim and decide on a left- or right-sided test
Determine the rejection region for α = 5 % with a cumulative table
Formulate the decision and explain why 'not rejected' does not mean 'proven'
topics.assessmentPrompt: A company claims at most 10 % of its parts are faulty. Can {{name}} design a test with 100 parts at the 5 % level and say what result would lead them to reject the claim?

prerequisites.reason: Rejection regions are found with cumulative probabilities
The expected value indicates where results should lie

topics.laenderNotes: KMK alternative B2 (eA). Leistungskurs only in BW and Berlin/Brandenburg; Bayern for all students (Jgst. 12); no longer in the NRW plan since 2023; not in NI.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Type I and type II errors
topics.description: Describe the two possible wrong decisions of a test (rejecting a true null hypothesis, keeping a false one) in context, calculate their probabilities for given alternatives, and discuss how significance level and sample size affect both errors.
evidence: Describe type I and type II errors in the context of a given test
Calculate the probability of a type II error for a specific alternative p
Explain the trade-off between the two errors and the effect of a larger sample
topics.assessmentPrompt: For a test of a new medicine, can {{name}} explain which error would be worse for patients and how the test could be changed to make it less likely?

prerequisites.reason: The errors belong to a test decision

topics.laenderNotes: Taught with hypothesis tests: Bayern (all students), BW Leistungsfach, Berlin/Brandenburg Leistungskurs.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Continuous random variables
topics.description: Distinguish discrete from continuous random variables (e.g. waiting times, body heights), describe continuous distributions by a density function whose integral over an interval gives a probability, and use the distribution function as an integral function.
evidence: Classify random variables in contexts as discrete or continuous
Check whether a function is a probability density (non-negative, total area 1)
Calculate P(a ≤ X ≤ b) as an integral and explain why P(X = a) = 0
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the probability that a person is exactly 1.80000 m tall is zero, while the probability of being between 1.75 m and 1.85 m is not?

prerequisites.reason: Continuous variables extend the concept of a random variable
Probabilities are areas under the density

topics.laenderNotes: KMK eA; BW includes the discrete/continuous distinction in the Basisfach too; Bayern for all students (Jgst. 13).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Normal distribution
topics.description: Use the bell-shaped normal distribution with parameters μ and σ to model measurements and approximately binomial situations, calculate probabilities with a digital tool, interpret the σ-intervals and judge when a normal model is appropriate.
evidence: Describe how μ and σ change position and shape of the bell curve
Calculate interval probabilities for a normally distributed variable with a calculator
Judge whether a data set or a binomial distribution can be approximated by a normal distribution
topics.assessmentPrompt: If the weight of bags of flour is normally distributed with μ = 1,000 g and σ = 8 g, can {{name}} work out what share of bags weighs less than 990 g?

prerequisites.reason: The normal distribution is a continuous distribution
Binomial histograms approach the bell shape
The density is built from e^(−x²/2)

topics.laenderNotes: Leistungskurs only in NRW, NI and Berlin/Brandenburg; BW Basisfach with digital tools but no density; Bayern for all students.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child calculates with positive and negative fractions and decimals, solves everyday percentage problems such as discounts and VAT, and works out simple and compound interest.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind rechnet mit positiven und negativen Brüchen und Dezimalzahlen, löst Prozentaufgaben aus dem Alltag wie Rabatt und Mehrwertsteuer und berechnet Zinsen und Zinseszinsen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child meets square roots and irrational numbers such as √2 and π, uses powers with negative and fractional exponents and scientific notation, and learns logarithms to solve growth questions.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Quadratwurzeln und irrationale Zahlen wie √2 und π kennen, nutzt Potenzen mit negativen und gebrochenen Exponenten und die Zehnerpotenzschreibweise und löst mit Logarithmen Wachstumsfragen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child calculates areas of trapezia and polygons, volumes and surfaces of prisms, and discovers the number π to work out the circumference and area of circles.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind berechnet Flächen von Trapezen und Vielecken, Volumen und Oberfläche von Prismen und entdeckt die Kreiszahl π, um Umfang und Fläche von Kreisen zu bestimmen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child calculates arcs and sectors and the volume and surface of cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres, also for composite real objects, and learns radian measure.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind berechnet Kreisbögen und Kreisausschnitte sowie Volumen und Oberfläche von Zylindern, Pyramiden, Kegeln und Kugeln, auch bei zusammengesetzten Gegenständen, und lernt das Bogenmaß kennen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child simplifies and expands algebraic terms (including the binomial formulas), solves linear equations and systems of two equations, and describes proportional and linear relationships with tables, graphs and functions.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind vereinfacht Terme und multipliziert sie aus (auch mit binomischen Formeln), löst lineare Gleichungen und Gleichungssysteme und beschreibt proportionale und lineare Zusammenhänge mit Tabellen, Graphen und Funktionen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child works with quadratic, exponential, power and sine functions, solves quadratic equations with the formula, and chooses suitable function models for real processes such as growth or periodic change.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind arbeitet mit quadratischen Funktionen, Exponential-, Potenz- und Sinusfunktionen, löst quadratische Gleichungen mit der Lösungsformel und wählt passende Funktionsmodelle für reale Vorgänge wie Wachstum oder periodische Veränderungen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child uses angle theorems and congruence, constructs triangles with compass and ruler or software, and learns special lines and circles of triangles and Thales' theorem.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind nutzt Winkelsätze und Kongruenz, konstruiert Dreiecke mit Zirkel und Lineal oder Software und lernt besondere Linien und Kreise im Dreieck sowie den Satz des Thales kennen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child uses similarity, the intercept theorems, Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry (sine, cosine, tangent) to calculate lengths and angles in figures, solids and real situations.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind berechnet mit Ähnlichkeit, Strahlensätzen, dem Satz des Pythagoras und der Trigonometrie (Sinus, Kosinus, Tangens) Längen und Winkel in Figuren, Körpern und Sachsituationen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child describes data with median, quartiles and box plots, calculates Laplace probabilities, and uses tree diagrams and path rules for multistage random experiments.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind beschreibt Daten mit Median, Quartilen und Boxplots, berechnet Laplace-Wahrscheinlichkeiten und nutzt Baumdiagramme und Pfadregeln für mehrstufige Zufallsexperimente.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child works with two-way tables and conditional probabilities, plans fair surveys, and learns to judge statistics and risk statements in the media critically.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind arbeitet mit Vierfeldertafeln und bedingten Wahrscheinlichkeiten, plant faire Umfragen und lernt, Statistiken und Risikoangaben in den Medien kritisch zu beurteilen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child learns to write simple mathematical proofs, to check statements and their converses, and to use spreadsheets and dynamic geometry software as everyday maths tools.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, einfache mathematische Beweise zu führen, Aussagen und ihre Umkehrungen zu prüfen und Tabellenkalkulation und dynamische Geometriesoftware als Werkzeuge zu nutzen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child meets proofs by contradiction and learns to judge mathematical models critically, comparing their assumptions with reality and improving them.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt indirekte Beweise kennen und beurteilt mathematische Modelle kritisch, indem es ihre Annahmen mit der Wirklichkeit vergleicht und sie verbessert.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your teenager learns calculus: rates of change and derivatives, investigating functions and solving optimisation problems, exponential growth models, and integrals to calculate areas and reconstruct totals; Leistungskurs students add the chain rule, logarithm functions and volumes of revolution.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Differential- und Integralrechnung: Änderungsraten und Ableitungen, Funktionsuntersuchungen und Optimierungsaufgaben, Wachstumsmodelle mit der e-Funktion sowie Integrale zur Flächen- und Bestandsberechnung; im Leistungskurs kommen Kettenregel, ln-Funktion und Rotationskörper hinzu.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your teenager describes points, lines and planes in space with vectors, solves linear systems, and calculates intersections and angles with the dot product; Leistungskurs students also calculate distances in space.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind beschreibt Punkte, Geraden und Ebenen im Raum mit Vektoren, löst lineare Gleichungssysteme und berechnet Schnittpunkte und Winkel mit dem Skalarprodukt; im Leistungskurs kommen Abstandsberechnungen hinzu.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your teenager works with conditional probability, random variables, expected value and the binomial distribution; Leistungskurs students add hypothesis tests, confidence intervals and the normal distribution.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind arbeitet mit bedingten Wahrscheinlichkeiten, Zufallsgrößen, Erwartungswert und Binomialverteilung; im Leistungskurs kommen Hypothesentests, Konfidenzintervalle und die Normalverteilung hinzu.
